> Can confirm the exact same behavior on OpenAI-compatible streaming clients (`muse-spark-1.2-contributor` via `/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`).
> 
> When streaming responses, the gateway closes the SSE stream without `choices[0].finish_reason: "stop"`. >

`E_ACCESSDENIED` on WSL instance creation is almost never the bash tool itself, it's that no WSL distro is set as default or the WSL service can't come up for the Desktop process. Since `wsl` from PowerShell throws the same thing, check `wsl --status` and `wsl --set-default <distro>` first, and if the service looks dead, `wsl --shutdown` then `wsl --update` usually brings it back. Getting a default distro set should unblock the hard-coded `bash.exe` path. Also worth filing the shell-selector ask so Desktop stops assuming WSL in the first place.

Update: the unbounded native-library temp-file growth described here is fixed in OpenCode V2.

As of V2 build `0.0.0-dev-17643`, the compiled CLI uses **Bun 1.4.0-canary.1 (`681a49bee`)**. That runtime includes [oven-sh/bun#29587](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/29587), which replaces the unique temporary `.so`/`.dylib`/`.node` extraction on every load with a deterministic, content-hashed path reused across calls, Workers, processes, and restarts. The V2 build provenance is [workflow run 32216069554](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/32216069554).

This bounds extraction to one reusable file per embedded native module and user instead of allowing unbounded disk growth. It does not mean the temp directory will contain zero native files, and upgrading does not remove files leaked by older builds; those stale randomly named files can be cleaned up after all older OpenCode processes have stopped.

That runtime includes [oven-sh/bun#29587](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/pull/29587), which replaces the unique temporary `.so`/`.dylib`/`.node` extraction on every load with a deterministic, content-hashed path reused across calls, Workers, processes, and restarts. The V2 build provenance is [workflow run 32216069554](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/32216069554).

This bounds extraction to one reusable file per embedded native module and user instead of allowing unbounded disk growth. It does not mean the temp directory will contain zero native files, and upgrading does not remove files leaked by older builds; those stale randomly named files can be cleaned up after all older OpenCode processes have stopped.

I would like to propose the following UX for this feature:

- Use the user-facing term **Split**.
- Show a Split icon immediately after the existing Copy icon on completed assistant responses.
- Clicking Split opens a dialog titled **Continue in a new session**.
- Its description reads: **Continue from this message in a new session**.
- Selecting it creates an independent session containing the conversation through the selected assistant response, inclusively.
- Messages after the selected response are excluded.
- Tool results, attachments, and relevant context are preserved.
- No Git branch is created.
- The original session remains unchanged.
- OpenCode navigates to the new session after creation.

This supports side tasks and alternative approaches without contaminating the original session context. It should work in both the web and desktop apps through their shared UI.

The scope is intentionally limited to Split. It does not add feedback buttons or other message actions.
